cd /Users/carter/dev/approval-md/.claude/worktrees/aprv-149-finish && git add .github/workflows/ci.yml README.md scripts/run-tests.mjs tests/ci-guard.test.ts && git commit -F - <<'MSGEOF'
APRV-149: CI compiles once, the suite shards, and the Node floor moves to the queue

The full gate cost roughly nine to ten minutes and every landed PR paid it
twice, once on pull_request and again as a merge-queue candidate. Three
sources of waste, all removed here, none of them the gate itself.

tsc ran three times per full-gate job: `npm run build`, then `npm test`
(`tsc && node scripts/run-tests.mjs`), then `npm run typecheck` (`tsc
--noEmit`). The second and third passes cannot fail where the first passed.
The job now builds and then invokes the runner directly on what it built.
package.json is untouched, so `npm test` keeps its build-then-run shape for
humans, who have not already built.

The suite ran as one `node --test` pool over 94 files on two runner cores.
`scripts/run-tests.mjs --shard <k>/<n>` takes the file at sorted position i
into shard (i mod n) + 1, and the full job is now a three-shard matrix on
Node 22, so the tier's wall clock is the slowest shard. The assignment is
exhaustive and non-overlapping by construction, and the runner says why in
a comment rather than leaving it assumed; an out-of-range index, an empty
shard, a malformed spec, and `--shard` with `--only` are hard errors, since
a shard scheme that quietly drops a file turns a green matrix into no
evidence at all.

The Node 20 floor now runs where it decides something: unsharded, on
merge_group and on pushes to main. `engines.node` is >=20 and the floor is
the version nobody develops on, so it stays in the gate; a pull request no
longer waits for a second whole suite to repeat what the shards said, and
nothing becomes main without the floor having run on it.

The required `ci` aggregator needs the shard matrix (GitHub reports one
result for a matrix job, `success` only when every shard succeeded) and the
floor leg. Because the floor leg is conditional, the aggregator computes
FLOOR_REQUIRED from the same event condition the job runs under: the queue
and pushes to main require success, every other event requires skipped or
success. Skipped-when-required stays a failure for every tier. The
classifier and the light and records tiers are unchanged.

The CI guard's pins move to the new shape without weakening what they hold:
both Node majors are still asserted, the shard axis must be exactly 1..n
with a denominator matching the matrix size, the compile-once property is
asserted as the absence of `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` from both
full-tier jobs, and selection is tested as a partition over the real
discovered list and over synthetic ones, with every non-partition request
spawned and required to refuse.

Local: 2311 tests pass in 202.0 s unsharded; shards of 32/31/31 files run
749/606/956 tests in 57.2/91.6/84.1 s, summing to the whole suite exactly.
AC5 (measured before/after wall clock) stays open until this runs in CI.

MSGEOF
